positions.name: DirectiveKnowledgeErasure
positions.frame: Is the speaker commanding erasure or suppression of knowledge from the record, asserting authority over what may be retained?
positions.why: All three expressions cohere under one directional read: the speaker enacts authority-ranking control over what the record may hold. src-1 and src-2 are imperatives demanding total erasure of specific knowledge (Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove's work), while src-3 is a flat assertive that ratifies the directive's premise by claiming the observatory never performed the calibration. The set holds a tension between performed command (src-1, src-2) and asserted fact (src-3) — one is instruction, the other is justification — but both serve the same authority move over what may be retained.
